newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - Iraq aids modest recovery.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - Iraq aids modest recovery.

text.p: Mounting tensions in oil-rich Iraq will combine with improved refining margins and a cautious resumption of transatlantic trade to bring some relief to sellers of physical crude oil in Europe this week, traders said.

Brent futures gained nearly 90 cents a barrel on Monday in reaction to the indefinite delay of the implementation of a limited Iraqi oil sale in response to Baghdad's attack on the capital of its northern Kurdish province.
But any gains in physical differentials were likely to be modest, traders said.
"The tone is firmer - products are pretty strong and barrels are moving to the U.S. again," said a North Sea trader.

Shipping brokers said Swiss-based trader Vitol fixed the Berge Banker to take 285,000 tonnes of Brent crude from Sullom Voe to the U.S. Gulf loading on September 12, helping to underpin Brent despite an overhang of unsold cargoes.
Five Brents loading September 14-18 were clocked on Friday.
Other North Sea grades were expected to benefit from a swift recovery in refinery economics, driven in part by stronger oil product prices, which banished all talk of throughput cuts.
"We're seeing pretty good margins in northwest Europe and the Mediterranean at the moment," said a producer/refiner.
The Brent-gas oil spread -- a rough measure of refining margins -- gained 70 cents last week to stand at $5.25 a barrel.
"Margins are looking brighter with gas oil and fuel picking up a bit. It's certainly off the bottom but whether people will now come out and buy is a different matter," said a trader.
Minor delays to North Sea loadings and the indefinite delay of Iraq's oil-for-food scheme also brightened the picture.
"The outlook has changed from half full to half empty - there's still the same amount of crude about but there's been a shift in sentiment," said an oil company trader.
All Forties cargoes scheduled for the second half of September will load a day late due to Enterprise's decision to bring forward maintenance at its Nelson field.
Nelson, which usually pumps about 160,000 barrels per day (bpd), will be closed from September 12 to September 24.
Norwegian Ekofisk cargoes due to load in the second decade of September have also been delayed by a day due to lower than expected production, trading sources said.
Mediterranean sellers drew particular comfort from the delay in the Iraqi crude deal since the bulk of the Iraqi exports would be sold from the Turkish Med port of Ceyhan.
Med benchmark Russian Urals crude due to load Sept 7-10 traded last Thursday at Dated Brent less $1.03 a barrel, seven cents firmer than the previous deal.
"If I had a (Sept) 15-20 loader I'd certainly be trying to get a better number," said a trader.
The outlook for West African crudes was bleaker, with light Nigerian grades like Qua Iboe and Bonny Light under particular pressure from ample unsold barrels, traders said.
